Alice: quick q — before I file the client PR: for the /rerank endpoint do we guarantee stable ordering when scores tie? if so what field is the canonical tiebreaker? also how should clients interpret null/NaN scores?

Ben: short answer: server should be deterministic but clients should not rely on insertion-order stability. we use an explicit fallback: `tie_breaker` field when present, otherwise deterministic hash of `item_id`.

Carla: +1 to explicit field. proposed response shape (simplified):
```json
{
  "model_version": "v2.1",
  "results": [
    {"id": "item-42", "score": 0.92, "tie_breaker": "3f1a2b"},
    {"id": "item-7",  "score": 0.92, "tie_breaker": "9b4c01"}
  ]
}
```
clients: sort by `score` desc, then by `tie_breaker` lexicographically if present. if `tie_breaker` missing, server guarantees deterministic but unspecified hash order.

Dinesh: how do we want to treat `null` scores? some older clients expect a numeric `score` field always present.

Carla: two options: (A) always include `score`, fill `null` => treat as lowest priority (place after any numeric scores) but keep deterministic order via `tie_breaker`/hash; (B) include `score` only when computed and add `unscored: true` flag. my vote: (A) for backward compat, plus add `score_is_estimated` or `score_source` for clarity.

Ben: agree with (A). server implementation note: treat NaN as -Inf for ordering, but write literal `null` in JSON to signal unknown. add metric `rerank.score_null_count`.

Erin: rollout plan: ship response field but make clients tolerant. Canary on 10% traffic for 48h. header opt-in to preserve legacy behavior: `X-Rerank-Compat: legacy` returns `score` as 0.0 for legacy clients and omits `tie_breaker`. new default returns `null` for unknown and includes `tie_breaker`. we should document this clearly in the API spec.

Alice: @Carla can you add a sample backwards-compatible snippet in the spec? @Ben do you want to own the client PR to prefer `tie_breaker` when present?

Carla: on it, will add examples and a small note about deterministic hashing seed (server-side only).

Ben: I can take the client changes. will handle tests for stable ordering and null-score acceptance.

Erin: telemetry items to add: `rerank.tie_breaker_used`, `rerank.score_null_count`, `rerank.legacy_header_hits`. also add an eval to ensure we don't regress ordering for top-k.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: /services/rerank v2.1 -> cluster-a (10%). :rocket:

Alice: thanks all — i'll file the PRs: one for spec docs (Carla), one for client lib (Ben), and an infra canary plan (Erin). ping me if you need more details. :thumbsup:
